page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.2xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton Gen8 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the instance supplies 8 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 vCPU-to-core mapping. Memory allocation is balanced at 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4.0 GB per core). Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached volumes, while the network interface delivers a baseline throughput of 17 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive memory subsystem throughput, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3170.21 and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.46 GB/sec. General multi-core processing registers in the average bracket, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 10132.0 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 13648.52. In application workloads, the configuration achieves 17.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 19.98 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Performance tradeoffs center on specialized compute paths. While standard software compilation under Clang reaches 16230.0, the PassMark CPU encryption benchmark ranks in the bottom 25% at 1510.06. Similarly, large language model prompt processing on a 7B model settles into the bottom decile at 15.66 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of hardware accelerators. Cost efficiency remains aligned with balanced general-purpose workloads, offering predictable single-threaded core isolation and memory bandwidth without the expense of integrated NVMe or GPU silicon.

This hardware profile is well configured for containerized application tiers, microservices, mid-tier Redis caching, Clang continuous integration pipelines, and web application serving requiring dedicated core stability and steady 17 Gbps networking.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.2xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz and 32.0 GB of system memory. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 17 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and relies entirely on remote storage, as no local disks or hardware accelerators are present. Benchmarks demonstrate strong memory subsystem performance, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory result of 3170.21 and solid single-thread decompression speeds. General multi-core compute, web serving throughput of 19.98 GB/sec, and Redis operations perform squarely in the median tier. Lower results appear in cryptographic tests and medium-scale LLM inference prompt processing. This configuration offers predictable core density and bandwidth efficiency for microservices, CI build nodes, web serving, and distributed in-memory caching layers.
